title: Bank of America launches BankAmericard
summary: Bank of America introduced BankAmericard in Fresno, California, with a mass mailing of about 65,000 unsolicited cards. It was the first general-purpose consumer credit card.

title: Interbank Card Association formed
summary: Regional bank card associations joined to create Interbank, a bank-owned rival to BankAmericard. Marine Midland Bank's Karl Hinke led the Buffalo-based effort.

title: Master Charge brand launched
summary: The network took the name Master Charge: The Interbank Card. It adopted the overlapping red and yellow circles after First National Bank of California joined.

title: National BankAmericard Inc. formed
summary: Bank of America gave up control of the program, and issuing banks set up National BankAmericard Inc. with Dee Hock as president and CEO.

title: First electronic authorization system
summary: National BankAmericard launched the first electronic authorization system, followed by electronic clearing and settlement.

title: BankAmericard becomes Visa
summary: BankAmericard and its licensees such as Barclaycard and Carte Bleue adopted the single name Visa, which sounds the same in every language.

title: Renamed MasterCard
summary: Master Charge was renamed MasterCard, dropping the Interbank name.

title: Global ATM network launches
summary: Visa launched an ATM network giving cardholders round-the-clock cash access worldwide.

title: Sears launches the Discover Card
summary: Sears introduced the Discover Card in a 1985 trial, with the first purchase on September 17 at an Atlanta Sears. It had no annual fee and offered cash back, and the national rollout followed in 1986.

title: Maestro debit network launched
summary: MasterCard and Europay International partnered to launch Maestro, a global point-of-sale debit network.

title: Sears spins off Dean Witter, Discover & Co.
summary: Sears spun off its financial services unit, which included the Discover Card business, as a public company named Dean Witter, Discover & Co.

title: Visa check card and EMV specifications
summary: Visa introduced its check card (debit) and co-created the EMV chip card specifications for interoperability.

title: Merger with Morgan Stanley
summary: Dean Witter, Discover & Co. merged with Morgan Stanley. The combined firm was called Morgan Stanley Dean Witter, Discover & Co., and Discover was part of Morgan Stanley until 2007.

title: Merger with Europay International
summary: MasterCard International merged with Europay International and became a Delaware corporation.

title: Acquisition of the PULSE network
summary: Discover bought the PULSE interbank debit network for about $311 million. This began its build-out as a payments network as well as a card issuer.

title: IPO on the NYSE
summary: MasterCard went public on 25 May 2006 at $39 per share under the ticker MA. It had previously been owned by its member banks.

title: Spin-off from Morgan Stanley
summary: Morgan Stanley completed the spin-off of Discover, which became an independent public company named Discover Financial Services.

title: Global restructuring into Visa Inc.
summary: Regional Visa businesses were merged into a single corporation, Visa Inc., in preparation for going public. Visa Europe stayed separate and member-owned.

title: Antitrust settlement and Diners Club purchase
summary: Discover received a $2.75 billion settlement from Visa and Mastercard in its antitrust case. It also acquired Diners Club International from Citigroup for about $165 million.

title: Record IPO
summary: Visa went public on March 18, raising $17.9 billion, later about $19.1 billion with the overallotment. It was then the largest IPO in U.S. history.

title: Student Loan Corporation acquisition
summary: Discover acquired Citigroup's Student Loan Corporation, which expanded its student lending business. The deal was finalized in December 2010.

title: VocaLink acquisition and rebrand
summary: Mastercard bought UK payments infrastructure firm VocaLink for about $920M. The same year it adopted the "Mastercard" spelling with a new logo.

title: Visa Europe acquired
summary: Visa Inc. completed its acquisition of Visa Europe on June 21 and reunified its operations globally.

title: EU interchange fine and wordmark-free logo
summary: The European Commission fined Mastercard EUR 570.5M for interchange fee violations. The same year Mastercard removed text from its logo, leaving only the overlapping circles.

title: Plaid acquisition abandoned
summary: The US Department of Justice challenged Visa's planned $5.3 billion purchase of Plaid. Visa and Plaid abandoned the deal in January 2021.

title: Capital One announces $35.3 billion deal
summary: On February 19, 2024, Capital One announced an all-stock acquisition of Discover valued at about $35.3 billion. Shareholders of both companies approved it on February 18, 2025.

title: Recorded Future acquisition
summary: Mastercard acquired threat-intelligence firm Recorded Future for about $2.65B, a major move into cybersecurity.

title: Capital One closes the Discover acquisition
summary: After approval from the Federal Reserve and the OCC in April 2025, Capital One closed the deal on May 18, 2025. It said Discover-branded cards would continue, along with the PULSE and Diners Club networks.
